_comment: Run template for nist-ibal: chiller 1 of the NIST IBAL lab plant, a nominal 5-ton R-410A water-cooled chiller, at a 15-minute resample (the store keeps 1-minute means of the 10-second export). The lab runs experiments, not a building: the chiller is staged, reset and cycled by each experiment's control code, and the store holds only the experiment hours (105 days of the full window; none between experiments). chiller_efficiency's design ceiling is CALIBRATED from the default window's 55 fully-on hours (median 1.12 kW/ton), not a generic value. The drift section runs the chiller family's refrigerant-side detectors on the two refrigerant quantities IBAL publishes in a form CAMBER can use -- discharge (head) and suction pressure, raw psig with the load from the chilled-water flow and temperatures; the subcooling, superheat and approach detectors decline because the export carries line temperatures, not the saturation-referenced differences CAMBER's roles need. The windows split the default export (baseline 2025-06-28 to 2025-07-01, current 2025-07-02 to 2025-07-09); freeze the baseline first with `camber drift freeze <config>` (a run never creates one), then `camber drift run <config>`. No refrigerant-side fault is documented for these windows, so every drift alarm here is a false alarm on normal operation -- the dataset measures specificity, not detection.
